description: The roles of an anaesthetic record, written with no hospital in mind. A hospital's map supplies each role view as one SELECT over its own tables, and an audit written against the role views then runs unchanged at any hospital. roles.md, beside this file, explains each role in words.
rules: One row of role_anaesthetic is one anaesthetic, and its key identifies that anaesthetic and no other.
Every time is in local time, as the hospital's clocks showed it, and no view converts a time to another zone.
A reading, an event, a drug given, a device, a fluid or a person present belongs to an anaesthetic by its link to that anaesthetic, and never because its time falls within the anaesthetic.
A laboratory result and a diagnosis belong to the patient and the stay, and an audit that wants those near an anaesthetic chooses its own window around it.
A note belongs to an anaesthetic by its link to that anaesthetic where the hospital's system makes one, and otherwise to the stay or to the patient.
A role view keeps the rows that an audit leaves out, such as test patients, anaesthetics with no stop and values that were not accepted, so that the counts can see them.
A role view never joins in a way that repeats a row of the thing it describes, so that the view's key identifies its row.
An empty value means that the record does not say, and a value that the record holds but cannot be read as the role's type is also empty.
A key compares equal with itself within one hospital only, and no key is carried from one hospital to another.

A value is in the unit that its role or its kind fixes, and a view converts a value held in another unit; only a drug's amount and a laboratory result of the kind other are given in the unit carried beside them.

views.name: role_patient
views.title: Patients
views.description: One row for each patient, test and training patients included, so that an audit can leave them out.
views.holds: The patient table of the hospital's system, which holds one row for each person; the date of death is often held in a second patient table or loaded from a registry.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the patient, the same value that role_anaesthetic.patient_key holds.
columns.holds: The patient table's own key.

columns.name: birth_date
columns.title: date of birth
columns.meaning: The date of birth, to the day, so that an age in days counts calendar dates.
columns.holds: The patient table.

columns.name: death_date
columns.title: date of death
columns.meaning: The date of death where the hospital knows of it, and empty otherwise.
columns.holds: The patient table, a second patient table, or a table loaded from a death registry.

columns.name: is_test
columns.title: test patient
columns.meaning: 1 for a test or training patient who is not a real person, and 0 for every other patient.
columns.holds: A flag on the patient table or a second patient table, or a naming convention that the hospital uses for test patients.

views.name: role_anaesthetic
views.title: Anaesthetics
views.description: One row for each episode of anaesthesia or sedation given by an anaesthetist, including those whose start or stop is missing or out of order, so that the counts can see them.
views.holds: The anaesthetic record or anaesthesia episode, which is usually its own table, linked to a theatre case or to an encounter of its own.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the anaesthetic, the same value that role_reading.anaesthetic_key holds.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record's own key.
look_for: unique id of the anaesthesia episode

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient who had the anaesthetic, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record, or the encounter or theatre case to which it is linked.

columns.name: start_time
columns.title: start time
columns.meaning: When the anaesthetic started, in local time.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record, or the anaesthesia start event of the theatre case.

columns.name: stop_time
columns.title: stop time
columns.meaning: When the anaesthetic stopped, in local time, and empty where no stop was recorded.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record, or the anaesthesia stop event of the theatre case.

views.name: role_reading
views.title: Readings charted during an anaesthetic
views.description: One row for each value charted in an anaesthetic's own record, with its kind from the vocabulary below, including values that were not accepted and values that are not numbers.
views.one_row_per: value charted in an anaesthetic's record
views.holds: A table of measurements or observations, often the largest in the system, with one row for each value of each kind at each moment, reached from the anaesthetic through the record or sheet on which it was charted.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic whose record holds the reading, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The sheet or record on which the reading was charted, which carries the anaesthetic's key or the key of the anaesthetic's own encounter.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of reading
columns.meaning: What was measured, as one of the kinds of the vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the reading that points at the system's own list of the things that can be charted.

columns.name: reading_time
columns.title: time of the reading
columns.meaning: When the value was taken, in local time, and not when it was filed.
columns.holds: The reading itself, which often holds a second time at which the value was entered or received.

columns.name: value
columns.title: value
columns.meaning: The value as a number in the kind's own unit, and empty where the charted value is not a number.
columns.holds: The reading itself, usually as text that holds numbers and words alike.

columns.name: accepted
columns.title: accepted or rejected
columns.meaning: 1 where the value counts as valid, and 0 where it was marked as an artefact, rejected or superseded.
columns.holds: A flag on the reading, or the absence of the value after an edit, which the hospital's practice decides.

views.name: role_patient_detail
views.title: The patient's details at birth
views.description: One row for each patient whose record holds any of these details, for the covariates of an audit.
views.holds: A second patient table, the birth history of the child, or the delivery record of the mother when it is linked to the baby.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The table that holds the details.

columns.name: sex
columns.title: sex at birth
columns.meaning: The sex recorded at birth, as one of the kinds of the sex vocabulary.
columns.holds: The patient table, usually as a code with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: gestation_weeks
columns.title: gestation in weeks
columns.meaning: The gestational age at birth in weeks, with any days as a fraction of a week.
columns.holds: The birth history, the newborn's delivery record, or a measurement charted on the newborn.

columns.name: birth_weight_grams
columns.title: birth weight in grams
columns.meaning: The weight at birth in grams.
columns.holds: The birth history, the newborn's delivery record, or a measurement charted on the newborn.

views.name: role_stay
views.title: Hospital stays
views.description: One row for each hospital stay, from admission to discharge, day stays included, for the length of stay and for readmission.
views.holds: The hospital encounter or admission table, which holds the admission and the discharge of each stay.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the stay, the same value that role_anaesthetic_detail.stay_key holds.
columns.holds: The encounter's own key.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient whose stay it is, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The encounter table.

columns.name: admit_time
columns.title: admission time
columns.meaning: When the patient was admitted, in local time.
columns.holds: The encounter table.

columns.name: discharge_time
columns.title: discharge time
columns.meaning: When the patient was discharged, or died in hospital, in local time, and empty while the patient is still in hospital.
columns.holds: The encounter table.

columns.name: unplanned
columns.title: unplanned admission
columns.meaning: 1 for an emergency or other unplanned admission, 0 for a planned one, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The admission type or admission category of the encounter, as a code with a lookup table of names.

views.name: role_anaesthetic_detail
views.title: The anaesthetic's details
views.description: One row for each anaesthetic whose record holds any of these details, for the covariates and outcomes of an audit.
views.holds: Partly the anaesthetic record and partly the theatre case or surgical log, with the pre-anaesthetic assessment for the grade and the weight.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record's own key.
look_for: unique id of the anaesthesia episode

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay in which the anaesthetic took place, as role_stay.stay_key, and empty where the anaesthetic belongs to no stay.
columns.holds: The theatre case or the anaesthetic record, which points at the admission, sometimes through a link table.

columns.name: technique
columns.title: technique
columns.meaning: The kind of anaesthetic, as one of the kinds of the technique vocabulary.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record or the theatre case, usually as a code, and sometimes several for one anaesthetic.

columns.name: asa_grade
columns.title: ASA grade
columns.meaning: The ASA physical status grade from 1 to 6, without any letter for an emergency.
columns.holds: The pre-anaesthetic assessment, the anaesthetic record or the theatre case, usually as a code with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: is_emergency
columns.title: emergency operation
columns.meaning: 1 where the operation was done as an emergency, 0 where it was planned, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The theatre case or booking, or an E after the ASA grade.

columns.name: weight_kg
columns.title: weight in kilograms
columns.meaning: The patient's weight at the anaesthetic in kilograms.
columns.holds: The pre-anaesthetic assessment or a measurement charted on the day, and sometimes the theatre case.

columns.name: planned_icu
columns.title: planned intensive care
columns.meaning: 1 where intensive care after the operation was planned before it began, 0 where it was not, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The booking of the theatre case, as the planned destination after the operation or a request for an intensive care bed.

columns.name: unplanned_return
columns.title: unplanned return to theatre
columns.meaning: 1 where the operation was recorded as an unplanned return to theatre, 0 where it was not, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The theatre case, where the hospital records an unplanned return as a reason or a flag.

columns.name: height_cm
columns.title: height in centimetres
columns.meaning: The patient's height or length at the anaesthetic, in centimetres.
columns.holds: The pre-anaesthetic assessment or a measurement charted on the day, as the weight is.

columns.name: location
columns.title: location
columns.meaning: Where the anaesthetic was given, as one of the kinds of the location vocabulary.
columns.holds: The room or department of the theatre case or the anaesthetic record, whose kind the hospital's list of rooms or departments gives.

views.name: role_operation
views.title: Procedures done under an anaesthetic
views.description: One row for each procedure done under an anaesthetic, so that an anaesthetic for several procedures has several rows.
views.holds: The procedures of the theatre case or surgical log, with a lookup table of the procedures that the hospital offers.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic under which the procedure was done, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The theatre case, which the anaesthetic record points at, or a link table between the two.

columns.name: procedure_code
columns.title: procedure code
columns.meaning: The hospital's own code of the procedure, or a national code where the hospital uses one.
columns.holds: The procedures of the theatre case.

columns.name: procedure_name
columns.title: procedure name
columns.meaning: The name of the procedure as the hospital's list gives it.
columns.holds: The lookup table of procedures, or the theatre case itself.

columns.name: specialty
columns.title: surgical specialty
columns.meaning: The surgical specialty of the procedure, as one of the kinds of the specialty vocabulary, which gives the operation's kind.
columns.holds: The service or specialty of the theatre case or of the surgeon.

columns.name: is_cardiac
columns.title: cardiac procedure
columns.meaning: 1 where the procedure was a cardiac operation or a cardiac catheter procedure, 0 where it was not, and empty where nothing says.
columns.holds: The specialty of the theatre case, the procedure's own code, or a diagnosis of the stay.

views.name: role_unit_stay
views.title: Periods in a hospital unit
views.description: One row for each period that a patient spent in one unit during a hospital stay, for admission to intensive care after an anaesthetic.
views.holds: The movements of the encounter, with one row for each transfer in or out of a unit, and a lookup table that says what kind of unit each one is.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay during which the patient was in the unit, as role_stay.stay_key.
columns.holds: The movement row.

columns.name: unit_kind
columns.title: kind of unit
columns.meaning: The kind of unit, as one of the kinds of the unit vocabulary.
columns.holds: The department or unit of the movement, whose kind the hospital's list of units gives.

columns.name: entered_time
columns.title: time of entering the unit
columns.meaning: When the patient entered the unit, in local time.
columns.holds: The movement row.

columns.name: left_time
columns.title: time of leaving the unit
columns.meaning: When the patient left the unit, in local time, and empty while the patient is still there.
columns.holds: The next movement row of the same stay.

views.name: role_event
views.title: Milestones of an anaesthetic
views.description: One row for each timed milestone or complication of an anaesthetic, such as induction, intubation, incision, extubation, laryngospasm or arrival in recovery, with its kind from the event vocabulary.
views.holds: The events of the anaesthetic record or the timing events of the theatre case, each with a code for the kind of event; a complication may instead be held as a quality or incident record of the anaesthetic.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The event row, or the theatre case that it belongs to.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of milestone
columns.meaning: The kind of event, as one of the kinds of the event vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the event row with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: event_time
columns.title: time of the milestone
columns.meaning: When the event happened, in local time.
columns.holds: The event row.

views.name: role_drug
views.title: Drugs given
views.description: One row for each dose given during an anaesthetic, and for each start, change of rate and stop of an infusion.
views.holds: The administrations of the medication record, linked to their orders, or drug values charted on the anaesthetic record.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic during which the drug was given, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The order of the drug, which belongs to the anaesthetic's own encounter.

columns.name: drug
columns.title: drug
columns.meaning: The drug, as the hospital's own name or code for it.
columns.holds: The order, with a lookup table of the hospital's medications.

columns.name: action
columns.title: dose or infusion action
columns.meaning: What was done, as one of the kinds of the drug action vocabulary.
columns.holds: The administration row, as a code for the action.

columns.name: amount
columns.title: dose or rate
columns.meaning: The dose, or the rate of an infusion, as a number in the unit beside it.
columns.holds: The administration row.

columns.name: unit
columns.title: unit of the dose
columns.meaning: The unit of the amount, as the hospital records it.
columns.holds: The administration row, as a code for the unit.

columns.name: route
columns.title: route
columns.meaning: The route by which the drug was given, as the hospital records it.
columns.holds: The administration row or the order.

columns.name: given_time
columns.title: time given
columns.meaning: When the dose was given or the infusion changed, in local time.
columns.holds: The administration row, which often holds a second time at which it was charted.
look_for: time that the action took place

views.name: role_device
views.title: Devices placed
views.description: One row for each airway device, line or catheter placed for an anaesthetic, with its kind from the device vocabulary.
views.holds: The lines, drains and airways of the patient's record, each with its placement and removal.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic for which the device was placed, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The device row, where it carries the anaesthetic's key; otherwise the device belongs to the patient and the link must be found.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of device
columns.meaning: The kind of device, as one of the kinds of the device vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the device row with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: placed_time
columns.title: time placed
columns.meaning: When the device was placed, in local time.
columns.holds: The device row.

columns.name: removed_time
columns.title: time removed
columns.meaning: When the device was removed, in local time, and empty while it stays in place.
columns.holds: The device row.

columns.name: size
columns.title: size
columns.meaning: The size of the device as the hospital records it, such as the internal diameter of a tube or the gauge of a cannula.
columns.holds: The device row, or a property of the device charted as a measurement when it was placed.

columns.name: site
columns.title: site
columns.meaning: Where on the body the device was placed, as the hospital records it, such as the left radial artery or the right internal jugular vein.
columns.holds: The device row, often as a site and a side, or a property of the device charted when it was placed.

views.name: role_staff
views.title: Staff attending an anaesthetic
views.description: One row for each person who attended an anaesthetic, for each period in which that person was present, with their role and grade.
views.holds: The staff or providers of the anaesthetic record or the theatre case, each with a role and a start and end of responsibility, and the hospital's list of staff for the grade.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic that the person attended, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The staff row, or the theatre case that it belongs to.

columns.name: person_key
columns.title: the staff member's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the staff member, and never the person's name.
columns.holds: The staff row, as a key into the hospital's list of staff.
look_for: unique id of the staff member

columns.name: role
columns.title: role at the anaesthetic
columns.meaning: What the person did at the anaesthetic, as one of the kinds of the staff role vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the staff row with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: grade
columns.title: grade
columns.meaning: The person's grade at the time of the anaesthetic, as one of the kinds of the grade vocabulary.
columns.holds: The hospital's list of staff, as a provider type or a title; that list usually holds the grade today, and not the grade on the day.

columns.name: present_from
columns.title: time of joining
columns.meaning: When the person took over or joined the care of the patient, in local time.
columns.holds: The staff row.
look_for: start time of the staff member

columns.name: present_to
columns.title: time of leaving
columns.meaning: When the person handed over or left the care of the patient, in local time, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The staff row.
look_for: end time of the staff member

views.name: role_fluid
views.title: Fluids and blood products
views.description: One row for each volume of fluid or blood product given during an anaesthetic, and for each volume of blood or urine lost.
views.holds: The intake and output of the anaesthetic record, usually charted as measurements with a row for each kind of fluid, and the transfusion record for blood products.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic during which the fluid was given or lost, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The sheet or record on which the volume was charted, or the order of the blood product.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of fluid
columns.meaning: What was given or lost, as one of the kinds of the fluid vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the row with a lookup table of names, or the product code of a blood product.

columns.name: volume_ml
columns.title: volume in millilitres
columns.meaning: The volume given or lost, in millilitres, as one amount and not as a running total.
columns.holds: The row itself, often as text, and sometimes as a running total that the view must turn into amounts.

columns.name: given_time
columns.title: time given or measured
columns.meaning: When the volume was given or measured, in local time.
columns.holds: The row itself.

views.name: role_lab
views.title: Laboratory results
views.description: One row for each laboratory or point-of-care result for the patient, linked to the patient and the stay rather than to an anaesthetic.
views.holds: The results of the laboratory's orders, with one row for each component of each result, and the point-of-care and blood gas results that the hospital files with them.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient whose result it is, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The order of the test, or the encounter to which it belongs.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay during which the specimen was taken, as role_stay.stay_key, and empty where the result belongs to no stay.
columns.holds: The order of the test, which points at an encounter that is the stay or belongs to it.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of test
columns.meaning: What was measured, as one of the kinds of the laboratory vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the result for its component or test, with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: value
columns.title: result
columns.meaning: The result as a number in the kind's own unit, which the view converts to where the hospital holds another, and empty where the result is not a number.
columns.holds: The result row, often both as text and as a number.

columns.name: unit
columns.title: unit of the result
columns.meaning: The unit in which the hospital recorded the result, as it records it, so that a person can check the conversion.
columns.holds: The result row or the component's lookup table.

columns.name: taken_time
columns.title: time the specimen was taken
columns.meaning: When the specimen was taken, in local time, and not when the result was reported.
columns.holds: The result row or the specimen, which often hold the times of collection, receipt and result.

views.name: role_diagnosis
views.title: Coded diagnoses
views.description: One row for each coded diagnosis of the patient, from the coded discharge diagnoses, the problem list or the indication on the theatre booking.
views.holds: The coded diagnoses of the encounter or the hospital account, the patient's problem list, and the indication or diagnosis on the theatre booking, each with a lookup table of diagnoses.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient whose diagnosis it is, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The diagnosis row, or the encounter or problem list to which it belongs.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay for which the diagnosis was coded, as role_stay.stay_key, and empty for a problem-list entry that belongs to no stay.
columns.holds: The diagnosis row, as the key of the encounter or of the hospital account that belongs to the stay.

columns.name: code
columns.title: diagnosis code
columns.meaning: The diagnosis code, in the classification that the column beside it names.
columns.holds: The lookup table of diagnoses, which the diagnosis row points at, or the diagnosis row itself.

columns.name: code_system
columns.title: classification of the code
columns.meaning: The classification of the code, such as ICD-10-AM or SNOMED CT, or the hospital's own list.
columns.holds: The lookup table of diagnoses, or a fixed value where the hospital uses one classification only.

columns.name: name
columns.title: diagnosis name
columns.meaning: The name of the diagnosis as the hospital's list gives it.
columns.holds: The lookup table of diagnoses.

columns.name: is_principal
columns.title: principal diagnosis
columns.meaning: 1 where the diagnosis is the principal diagnosis of the stay, 0 where it is another, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: A flag or a sequence number on the diagnosis row, where the first line is the principal one.

columns.name: recorded_time
columns.title: time recorded
columns.meaning: When the diagnosis was noted or coded, in local time, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The diagnosis row or the problem-list entry, as the date noted or the date of entry.

views.name: role_note
views.title: Notes in the record
views.description: One row for each piece of free text in the record, such as a pre-anaesthetic assessment or an anaesthetic summary, with its text joined back into one value. A query that returns its text is an extract of identifying detail, and never a count.
views.holds: A notes table keyed by encounter with a note type, whose text is often split across several rows that the view joins back in order, and sometimes the comment fields of a structured form.

columns.name: note_key
columns.title: the note's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the note, the same value that role_finding.note_key holds.
columns.holds: The note's own key, or the key of the form whose comment field holds the text.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic to which the note belongs, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key, and empty where the system makes no link to one.
columns.holds: The note row, where it carries the anaesthetic's key or the key of the anaesthetic's own encounter.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient whose note it is, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The note row, or the encounter to which it belongs.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay to which the note belongs, as role_stay.stay_key, and empty where it belongs to no stay, such as a note of a clinic visit.
columns.holds: The note row, as the key of its encounter.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of note
columns.meaning: What kind of note it is, as one of the kinds of the note vocabulary.
columns.holds: A note type on the note row, with a lookup table of names that the hospital builds.

columns.name: written_time
columns.title: time written
columns.meaning: When the note was written or signed, in local time, and not when it was last edited.
columns.holds: The note row, which often holds the times of creation, signing and each edit.

columns.name: author_role
columns.title: author's grade
columns.meaning: The grade of the person who wrote the note, as one of the kinds of the grade vocabulary.
columns.holds: The author's provider type on the note row, or the hospital's list of staff.

columns.name: text
columns.title: text of the note
columns.meaning: The whole text of the note, with its lines joined back in order.
columns.holds: The lines of the note's text, each a row with a line number, or a single long text field.

views.name: role_finding
views.title: Facts found in the record
views.description: One row for each fact that the hospital's own process takes from a note or from a structured field, such as a Mallampati grade or the hours of fasting, with how it was found.
views.holds: The discrete answers of a structured pre-anaesthetic assessment or anaesthetic summary, which a map should find first, and otherwise a table that the hospital fills from its notes by rules, by a person or by a model run inside the hospital.

columns.name: note_key
columns.title: the note's identifier
columns.meaning: The note from which the fact was taken, as role_note.note_key, and empty for a fact taken from a structured field.
columns.holds: The answer row or the hospital's own table of findings.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic to which the fact belongs, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key, and empty where nothing links it to one.
columns.holds: The answer row, or the note from which the fact was taken.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient of whom the fact is true, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The answer row, or the note or encounter to which it belongs.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of fact
columns.meaning: What the fact is about, as one of the kinds of the finding vocabulary.
columns.holds: The question or element that the answer belongs to, with a lookup table of names that the hospital builds.

columns.name: value
columns.title: value of the fact
columns.meaning: The fact as text, such as 3 for a Mallampati grade, 6 for the hours of fasting, or yes or no for a history.
columns.holds: The answer row, often as text that holds numbers and words alike.

columns.name: method
columns.title: method of finding
columns.meaning: How the fact was found, as one of the kinds of the finding method vocabulary.
columns.holds: A fixed value for each source that the map reads, such as structured_field for the answers of a form.

columns.name: confidence
columns.title: confidence
columns.meaning: The confidence that the hospital's process gives the fact, from 0 to 1, and empty where it gives none, as for a structured field or a person's reading.
columns.holds: The hospital's own table of findings, where a rule or a model fills it.

columns.name: found_time
columns.title: time found
columns.meaning: When the fact was recorded in a structured field, or taken from the note, in local time.
columns.holds: The answer row, or the hospital's own table of findings.

types.key: Any type that compares equal with itself within one hospital, such as a whole number or text.
types.datetime: A date and a time of day, in local time.
types.number: A number that may hold a fraction.
types.flag: The whole number 1 or 0, and never empty.
types.flag_or_empty: The whole number 1 or 0, or empty where the record does not say.
types.kind: Text that is one of the kinds of the vocabulary that the column names.
types.text: Text as the hospital records it.

kinds.meaning: A mean arterial pressure from an arterial line, in mmHg.
A mean arterial pressure from a non-invasive cuff, in mmHg.
A heart rate, in beats a minute.
An oxygen saturation by pulse oximetry, in per cent.
An end-tidal carbon dioxide, in mmHg.
A body temperature, in degrees Celsius.
A systolic pressure from an arterial line, in mmHg.
A diastolic pressure from an arterial line, in mmHg.
A systolic pressure from a non-invasive cuff, in mmHg.
A diastolic pressure from a non-invasive cuff, in mmHg.
A central venous pressure, in mmHg.
A fraction of inspired oxygen, in per cent.
A positive end-expiratory pressure, in cmH2O.
An expired tidal volume, in millilitres.
A respiratory rate, in breaths a minute.
An end-tidal concentration of a volatile agent, in per cent, whichever agent it is.
A pain score, as a number on the scale that the hospital uses, usually from 0 to 10.
A blood glucose charted in the anaesthetic's record, usually from a bedside meter, in mmol/L.
Any other value charted in the anaesthetic's record, which the counts use to see whether the record is reached at all.

sex.meaning: Any other value, or one that says nothing was recorded.

technique.meaning: A general anaesthetic, with or without a regional block.
A regional or neuraxial block without a general anaesthetic.
Sedation given by an anaesthetist, including monitored anaesthesia care.
Local anaesthesia with an anaesthetist in attendance.
Any other kind, or one that the record does not give.

specialty.meaning: Cardiac surgery and cardiac catheter procedures.
Imaging and other procedures outside theatre.

unit.meaning: An intensive care unit, neonatal, paediatric or adult.
An operating theatre or a procedure room.

location.meaning: A radiology or imaging suite, such as for MRI or CT.
A cardiac or interventional catheter laboratory.
An intensive care unit, neonatal, paediatric or adult.
A ward or a procedure room on a ward.
Any other place, such as an endoscopy or oncology procedure room.

event.meaning: The airway placed or the trachea intubated.
A fall in oxygen saturation that the record marks as an event or complication.
A difficult mask ventilation, laryngoscopy or intubation recorded as such.
A cardiac arrest, or chest compressions started.
A drug error recorded against the anaesthetic.

device.meaning: A laryngeal mask or other supraglottic airway.
An epidural or other regional catheter.

drug_action.meaning: The rate of an infusion changed.
A dose that was charted but not given.

note.meaning: A pre-anaesthetic assessment, in a clinic, on the ward or on the day.
The anaesthetist's summary or record of the anaesthetic.
A note of the airway, such as of a difficult intubation, or an airway alert.
A note of a procedure done by the anaesthetist, such as a block or a central line.
The discharge summary of the stay.
A progress note on the ward or in intensive care.

finding.meaning: A difficult airway known or found, such as a difficult intubation at a previous anaesthetic.
The hours since the last solids or fluids, as the note gives them.
A problem at a previous anaesthetic.
A family history of a problem with anaesthesia, such as malignant hyperthermia or suxamethonium apnoea.
A named syndrome or genetic condition.
A cardiac history, such as congenital heart disease.
A respiratory history, such as asthma or prematurity with chronic lung disease.
A recent upper respiratory tract infection.
An allergy, as the note or the form gives it.

finding_method.meaning: Read from a discrete answer of a structured form.
Found by a pattern query over role_note that was tested on invented notes.
Found by a person reading the note.
Found by a model that the hospital chose to run inside the hospital.

staff_role.meaning: A surgeon or proceduralist, of any grade.
An anaesthetic nurse or anaesthetic technician who assisted the anaesthetist.
Any other person present, such as a scrub or scout nurse, a perfusionist or a student.

grade.meaning: A fellow, or a provisional fellow in the last year of training.
A registrar or other trainee in a specialty programme.
A resident medical officer or intern who is not in a specialty programme.
A nurse, including a nurse practitioner.
Any other grade, such as a technician or a student, or one that the record does not give.

fluid.meaning: A crystalloid, such as a balanced salt solution, saline or a dextrose solution.
A colloid, such as albumin or a starch or gelatin solution.
Fresh frozen plasma or another plasma product.
Blood salvaged from the operative field and returned to the patient.
Blood lost, as measured or estimated.
Any other fluid given or lost, such as a drain's output or a gastric aspirate.

lab.meaning: A glucose measured by the laboratory or a blood gas analyser, in mmol/L.
A pH, which has no unit.
A partial pressure of carbon dioxide, in mmHg.
A partial pressure of oxygen, in mmHg.
Any other result, in the unit beside it.

outcomes.name: death_within_days
outcomes.meaning: Whether the patient died within a given number of days of the anaesthetic's start, counted by calendar date.

outcomes.name: unplanned_intensive_care
outcomes.meaning: Whether the patient entered intensive care within 24 hours after the anaesthetic's stop, when intensive care had not been planned and the patient was not already there at the start.

outcomes.name: return_to_theatre_30_days
outcomes.meaning: Whether the same patient had another anaesthetic with an operation within 30 days after this one's stop, and whether the hospital recorded that return as unplanned.

outcomes.name: length_of_stay
outcomes.meaning: The time from admission to discharge of the stay in which the anaesthetic took place, and the time from the anaesthetic's stop to that discharge.

outcomes.name: readmission_30_days
outcomes.meaning: Whether the patient began another unplanned stay within 30 days after the discharge of the stay in which the anaesthetic took place.

outcomes.name: anaesthetic_complication
outcomes.meaning: Whether the anaesthetic's record holds any of the complications of the event vocabulary, such as laryngospasm, desaturation or cardiac arrest.

outcomes.name: transfusion
outcomes.meaning: Whether the patient was given red cells, platelets, plasma or cryoprecipitate during the anaesthetic, and how much in millilitres for each kilogram.

outcomes.name: recovery_time
outcomes.meaning: The time from arrival in recovery to discharge from recovery.

outcomes.name: postoperative_result
outcomes.meaning: A laboratory result, such as a lactate or a creatinine, in a window after the anaesthetic's stop that the audit chooses.
